propositions.text: The appellant is a citizen of Egypt appealing the RPD's April 25, 2019 decision rejecting his refugee claim.
propositions.quote: XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, a citizen of the Arab Republic of Egypt, is appealing the April 25, 2019, decision of the Refugee Protection Division (RPD) rejecting his claim for refugee protection.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant, an Egyptian citizen, appeals the RPD's April 25, 2019 refugee claim rejection, as stated by the court.

propositions.text: The appellant fears imprisonment and torture if returned to Egypt due to family monitoring and political activism.
propositions.quote: The appellant states that he fears being imprisoned and tortured if he returns to Egypt.

propositions.text: In 2013, military secret service investigated his brother and monitored family after brother left Egypt due to Muslim Brotherhood membership.
propositions.quote: in XXXX 2013, after his brother left the country because he was a member of the Muslim Brotherhood, the military secret service began investigating his brother and monitoring the movements of his family members.

propositions.text: Appellant left Egypt in 2016 to continue education in Canada, hosting an Egyptian activist against Sissi's regime.
propositions.quote: he left Egypt on XXXX XXXX, 2016, to continue his education in Canada. He indicates that, in Canada, he hosted an Egyptian who turned out to be an activist working against President Sissi's regime

propositions.text: Military officers visited appellant's parents in 2017 and 2018, warning about possible arrest warrants for appellant.
propositions.quote: military officers went to see his parents twice, once in XXXX 2017 and again in XXXX 2018. They asked about his activities in Canada against the regime in place and warned his parents that an arrest warrant could be issued for him.

propositions.text: Appellant decided to claim refugee protection in April 2018 after last military visit to parents.
propositions.quote: After this last incident, the appellant decided to claim refugee protection in April 2018.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant states he fears imprisonment and torture in Egypt due to family monitoring and activism, left Egypt in 2016, and claimed refugee protection in 2018.

propositions.text: The RPD rejected the appellant's refugee claim for lack of credibility.
propositions.quote: The RPD rejected the appellant's claim for refugee protection for lack of credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The RPD rejected the appellant's refugee claim for lack of credibility.

propositions.text: Egyptian authorities never told appellant's father he was accused of Muslim Brotherhood membership.
propositions.quote: The Egyptian authorities never told the appellant's father that he was accused of belonging to the Muslim Brotherhood.

propositions.text: Claimant cannot be held responsible for third party writings made in his absence; RPD failed to distinguish between father's statements and claimant's claim.
propositions.quote: The claimant cannot be held responsible for the writings of a third person made in his absence... The panel does not distinguish between what his father was told and what was reported by the claimant in his claim for refugee protection

propositions.text: RPD wrongfully rejected Egyptian documents based on simple contradiction with claimant's testimony.
propositions.quote: The RPD wrongfully rejected the documents of the Egyptian authorities on the basis of a simple contradiction of the claimant's testimony.

propositions.text: RPD lacked expertise to assess foreign documents and ignored presumption of truthfulness from Maldonado.
propositions.quote: the RPD did not have the expertise to assess the foreign documents" and ignored the presumption of truthfulness established in Maldonado.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD erred by misinterpreting father's statements, wrongly rejecting Egyptian documents, and ignoring presumption of truthfulness.

propositions.text: Appellant requests RAD to allow appeal, set aside RPD decision, and grant protected person status or refer for re-determination.
propositions.quote: allow this appeal, set aside the RPD determination... and grant the appellant the status of protected person; or set aside the RPD determination... and refer the matter to the RPD for re-determination.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant requests the RAD to allow the appeal, set aside the RPD decision, and grant protected status or refer for re-determination.

propositions.text: Appellant does not request to present new evidence or a hearing under subsections 110(4) or 110(6) of IRPA.
propositions.quote: The appellant is not requesting to present new evidence pursuant to subsection 110(4) of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act and does not want a hearing to be held under subsection 110(6) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant does not seek to present new evidence or a hearing under IRPA subsections 110(4) or 110(6).

propositions.text: Minister's representative did not intervene on appeal.
propositions.quote: The Minister's representative did not intervene on appeal.

paragraphs.summary: The Minister's representative did not intervene on appeal.

propositions.text: Pursuant to subsection 111(1)(a) IRPA, RAD confirms that appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.
propositions.quote: the RAD confirms the determination, namely, that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is not a "Convention refugee" or a "person in need of protection" within the meaning of sections 96 and 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD confirms the RPD's determination that the appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed.
propositions.quote: The appeal is dismissed

paragraphs.summary: The appeal is dismissed.

propositions.text: RAD must apply correctness standard of review to questions of fact, law, and mixed fact and law per Huruglica.
propositions.quote: In accordance with Huruglica, the RAD must apply the correctness standard of review to questions of fact, law and mixed fact and law.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD must apply the correctness standard of review to fact, law, and mixed questions per Huruglica.

propositions.text: Court conducted independent analysis of all evidence and hearing to determine correctness of RPD's decision.
propositions.quote: I have conducted an independent analysis of all the evidence on the record, after listening carefully to the hearing, in order to form my own opinion concerning this refugee protection claim and to determine whether the RPD's determination is correct.

paragraphs.summary: The court independently analyzed all evidence and hearing to assess correctness of the RPD decision.

propositions.text: After examining all evidence, RAD finds appellant not credible, agreeing with RPD.
propositions.quote: the RAD finds, as did the RPD, that the appellant is not credible.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the appellant not credible, agreeing with the RPD.

propositions.text: Appellant argues RPD failed to properly assess his credibility, affecting persecution risk.
propositions.quote: The appellant believes that the RPD failed to properly assess his credibility, and that the impact on the decision is such that the appellant would not be persecuted in his country.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD failed to properly assess his credibility, affecting the persecution risk finding.

propositions.text: The case's essence is based on the appellant's credibility.
propositions.quote: The very essence of this case is based on the appellant's credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The case fundamentally depends on the appellant's credibility.

propositions.text: Appellant's testimony was indirect and he did not answer panel's questions, undermining credibility.
propositions.quote: the appellant's testimony was indirect and he did not answer the panel's questions... This undermines his testimony and, therefore, his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The appellant's indirect testimony and failure to answer questions undermined his credibility.

propositions.text: Appellant said police never told his father he was accused of Muslim Brotherhood involvement; RPD noted contradiction with exhibits.
propositions.quote: the appellant pointed out that at no time did the police tell his father that he was accused of being a member of that group. The RPD noted a contradiction between the testimony and the content of certain exhibits

paragraphs.summary: Appellant said police never told his father of accusations; RPD noted contradiction with exhibits.

propositions.text: Appellant testified Egyptian authorities took his father and warned of appellant's possible arrest if he returned.
propositions.quote: the Egyptian authorities went to the family home on XXXX XXXX, 2018, took away the appellant's father and informed him that if the appellant returned to Egypt, he would be arrested.

propositions.text: Appellant's father informed him of the warning, prompting refugee claim.
propositions.quote: When told this, the appellant's father immediately informed his son, who filed a claim for protection.

paragraphs.summary: Appellant testified authorities took his father and warned of his arrest; father informed appellant, who filed claim.

propositions.text: Documents are crucial; appellant testified no legal concerns except arrest warrant without sentence mention.
propositions.quote: The documents submitted are of the utmost importance... he has no legal concerns other than the warrant... He added that he could be arrested at any time with the warrant.

paragraphs.summary: Documents are crucial; appellant testified only legal concern is arrest warrant without sentence mention.

propositions.text: Exhibit P-2 accuses appellant of Muslim Brotherhood activities; appellant denies membership, blaming brother.
propositions.quote: Exhibit P-2, where the Egyptian authorities accuse him of several things including disturbing the peace... He stated: "they say that I am part of the Muslim Brotherhood. I am not a member... it is my brother who is a member."

paragraphs.summary: Exhibit P-2 accuses appellant of Muslim Brotherhood activities; appellant denies membership, blaming brother.

propositions.text: Member confronted appellant about warrant for seven-year sentence; appellant said it was issued in his absence and misunderstood question.
propositions.quote: The member confronted him with his negative responses... even though it states in the warrant that he must serve a seven-year sentence. The appellant answered as follows: "it was issued in my absence...I misunderstood the question, I'm sorry...I don't know what would be said about me."

paragraphs.summary: Appellant was confronted about warrant for seven-year sentence; he said it was issued in his absence and misunderstood question.

propositions.text: The RAD must reject the appellant's explanations about his own arrest warrant due to inconsistencies and lack of explanation for charges.
propositions.quote: The RAD must reject the appellant's explanations about his own arrest warrant. His testimony is not consistent with his evidence, and he provided no explanation for the charges against him.

propositions.text: Egyptian authorities consider the appellant a Muslim Brotherhood member, a banned terrorist group in several countries.
propositions.quote: According to the evidence he submitted, the Egyptian authorities consider the appellant to be a member of the Muslim Brotherhood, a group that is banned in several countries as it is considered to be a terrorist group that has committed many abuses against the civilian population and governments.

propositions.text: Appellant only said his brother was a member of the terrorist group, contradicting his submitted evidence.
propositions.quote: The only thing he told the panel was that his brother was a member of this terrorist group. His testimony is clearly at odds with the evidence he submitted.

propositions.text: Main sensitive information is missing from appellant's written account and testimony, undermining his credibility.
propositions.quote: It should be noted that the main, consequential and sensitive information in his evidence is not found in his written account in the BOC Form or in his testimony. He denied or minimized the information contained in his documents. This considerably undermines his credibility.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the appellant's explanations about his arrest warrant inconsistent and lacking, notes Egyptian authorities consider him a Muslim Brotherhood member, and finds his credibility undermined.

propositions.text: The RAD finds that the RPD did not err.
propositions.quote: Consequently, the RAD finds that the RPD did not err.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD concludes the RPD did not err.

propositions.text: Appellant argues Egyptian documents were wrongly rejected and RPD lacks expertise to assess foreign documents, disregarding presumption of truthfulness.
propositions.quote: The second element concerns the Egyptian authorities' documents, which according to the appellant were wrongly rejected. He adds that [translation] "the RPD does not have the expertise to assess foreign documents" and disregarded the presumption of truthfulness established by the jurisprudence.

propositions.text: RPD granted no weight to exhibits contradicted by appellant, including docket and two authority reports.
propositions.quote: The RPD stated the following at paragraph 26 of its decision: [translation] "The panel grants no weight to the exhibits that he contradicted above, namely, the docket and the two reports by the authorities."

paragraphs.summary: The appellant argues the RPD wrongly rejected Egyptian documents and lacks expertise, while the RPD found no weight to contradicted exhibits.

propositions.text: Appellant misunderstands RPD's role; RPD did not assess document authenticity but did not grant probative weight to them.
propositions.quote: The RAD is of the opinion that the appellant's statement about the documents from Egypt shows that there is a misunderstanding. The appellant states that the panel does not have the expertise to assess the foreign documents whereas the RPD did not grant them any probative weight. Those are two different things.

propositions.text: Only experts can analyze documents for authenticity using specialized knowledge and tools.
propositions.quote: The RPD cannot state that a certain document is false or a forgery. It does not have the expertise to do so. Only an expert with their tools can analyze the paper, ink and typeset, among other things, and use their specialized knowledge to draw conclusions.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the appellant misunderstands the RPD's role, which cannot assess document authenticity but can assign probative weight; only experts can verify authenticity.

propositions.text: RPD did not conclude Egyptian documents were false or forgeries and did not assess their medium or presentation.
propositions.quote: In this case, the RPD did not conclude that the Egyptian documents submitted were false or forgeries. On the contrary, the RPD did not weigh in on the materials or the medium on which the documents are printed or presented.

propositions.text: RPD assigned no weight to documents after considering testimony and explanations; RAD agrees.
propositions.quote: After listening to and weighing the testimony and the appellant's explanations, the RPD stated that it did not assign any weight to the documents submitted. The RAD shares that opinion.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the RPD did not deem Egyptian documents false but assigned no weight after considering testimony, agreeing with that approach.

propositions.text: The RAD finds that the RPD did not err.
propositions.quote: Consequently, the RAD finds that the RPD did not err.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD concludes the RPD did not err.

propositions.text: The RAD finds the RPD rendered the correct decision for reasons set out in this decision.
propositions.quote: For the reasons set out in this decision, the RAD finds that the RPD rendered the correct decision.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD finds the RPD rendered the correct decision.

propositions.text: The RAD confirms the RPD's determination that the appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection under IRPA.
propositions.quote: In light of all the facts cited above and after examining all the evidence, the RAD confirms the RPD's determination that XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX is not a "Convention refugee" under section 96 of the IRPA or a "person in need of protection" within the meaning of sections 97 of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: The RAD confirms the RPD's determination that the appellant is not a Convention refugee or person in need of protection under IRPA.

propositions.text: The appeal is dismissed.
propositions.quote: The appeal is dismissed (signed) Michel Jobin Michel Jobin September 1, 2020 Date

paragraphs.summary: The RAD dismisses the appeal.
